commit.message:
feat(core): a refused record of frozen extensions names the classes that differ

The record of the extensions frozen at build now keeps what its fingerprint
was computed from: the discovery settings and each bean class with its
checksum. A start whose fingerprint differs compares its own deployment
with the build's and its note names the bean classes added, removed or
changed since (ten by name, the others counted), instead of two opaque
fingerprints. A record written before it kept its classes is still used,
and its refusal note keeps the old text.

The container keeps logging the note at debug level: the embedding runtime
knows whether a refused record is expected and says it at its own level.

commit.message:
docs(agents): list the interfaces of normal-scoped synthetic beans in @ClientProxies

Vauban generates a client proxy at build from the classes it compiles, and
a synthetic bean has none: the freeze records its descriptor, not a proxy,
and a deployment that runs its extensions at start has no build step. The
container then built a java.lang.reflect.Proxy at every start, every call
through reflection, a slower boot, nothing ahead of time, and every
application printed the RUNTIME CODE GENERATION FALLBACK warning
(BUG-20261113-19: Noether's EntityManager and EntityManagerFactory).

The build compatible extension rules gain the one that avoids it: list
those interfaces in @io.vidocq.vauban.api.ClientProxies, on the
*-cdi-vauban extension or, for a container-neutral brick, on its Vidocq
runtime extension.

commit.message:
fix(processor): name @ClientProxies instead of loading it, for an older vauban-api on the processor path

The downstream Vidocq build of this branch failed in
vidocq-runtime-dirac-metrics-extension: "Provider
io.vidocq.vauban.processor.VaubanProcessor could not be instantiated". The
processor took the annotation's name from ClientProxies.class in a static
field, and that module's processor path held the published vauban-api,
without the type, through a codegen bundle built on it: Maven's
nearest-wins mediation picked it over the one vauban-processor depends on.

The processor names the type as a string, as it already does for
VaubanComponentProvider. OlderApiOnProcessorPathTest loads the processor
through a class loader that hides ClientProxies: red before, green now.

commit.message:
fix(processor): build-time client proxies for the interfaces of synthetic beans (BUG-20261113-19)

The processor generates the client proxy of a normal-scoped bean it sees,
an interface-typed producer included (a class that implements the
interface, #42). A synthetic bean has no class it sees, so the container
proxied one of an interface type with java.lang.reflect.Proxy at boot,
every call through Method.invoke, and the boot warning advised adding
vauban-processor, which the module already had. Every Noether application
on Vidocq showed it for the EntityManager and EntityManagerFactory beans of
its units.

@io.vidocq.vauban.api.ClientProxies lists the interfaces of the synthetic
beans an extension registers, on any class of a module compiled with the
processor. The processor generates for each the class a producer of that
interface gets, in the package of the annotated class, under the key the
container looks up, in that package's _VaubanComponents, which it now
writes for a module without a bean too. A producer of the same interface
in the same package shares the proxy. A listed type that is not a public
interface fails the compilation.

The boot warning lists the run-time proxy of a synthetic bean apart, with
the @ClientProxies advice, and gives the vauban-processor advice only when
another kind of class is listed.

Docs: concepts, "Client proxies of synthetic beans"; internals (the proxy
table and AOT compatibility); reference (vauban-api); What's new.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DQoEaJaTRT5QCChBF3qYFK

commit.message:
fix(build): generate the $$Intercepted subclass of a class an extension binds

The processor and vauban:generate decided which beans get a $$Intercepted
subclass from what the class carries: javac's model of the source, or the
compiled class by reflection. An interceptor binding an @Enhancement adds is in
neither, so the container defined the subclass at start, with the Class-File
API, instead of using generated code (BUG-20261113-13, seen with Humboldt's
@SpanBinding on @WithSpan methods, Vidocq/vidocq#546).

BceProcessor.boundByEnhancement lists the classes the @Enhancement
modifications bind, on the class, a method or a constructor, whichever
addAnnotation added the binding. Both front-ends generate the subclass of such
a class when the container can wrap it (InterceptionTargets.isWrappable).

commit.message:
fix(core): install the contexts of extensions before the startup events (BUG-20261113-18)

The VaubanContainer constructor fired @Initialized(ApplicationScoped.class)
and Startup, and the builder installed the contexts build compatible
extensions register (MetaAnnotations.addContext) on the container it
returned, so after them: a Startup observer calling a @TransactionScoped
bean failed the start with "No context registered for scope". The builder
now calls VaubanContainer.start() last, once the contexts, the supplied
factories and the module lookups are set.

Found by a Vidocq IT of persistence units per module. BUG.md also records
BUG-20261113-19, seen in the same run: a synthetic bean of an interface
type always takes the run-time client proxy.

commit.message:
fix(core): the fingerprint counts what the extensions see, not debug information

A jlink image is linked with --strip-debug by default. jlink removes
SourceFile, LineNumberTable, LocalVariableTable, LocalVariableTypeTable and
MethodParameters, and computes some StackMapTables again, so the image's
class bytes are not the build's. The fingerprint was a CRC32C of those
bytes: the image never matched the record its build wrote, and every
extension ran at start.

A bean class now counts by what the extensions see of it: its model, as
the index holds it and the language model shows it, without the parameter
names, written as one text that is the same on any JVM (annotation members
in name order, each value tagged). A build compatible extension also counts
by its code, since its method bodies are what it does: the constant pool,
and each method's bytecode and exception table, without the debug
attributes and the stack maps. Over the 322 classes of vauban-core, jlink
keeps the pool, the code arrays, max_stack, max_locals and the exception
tables identical, and changes 202 stack map tables.

A change to the body of a bean's method no longer invalidates the record:
no extension sees it.

BUG-20261113-17 (second cause).

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DQoEaLnfwGpxVYSXFoFQA8

commit.message:
fix(classloader): one record seen through two loaders is one record

In a jlink image, Vidocq finds the application module in the boot layer and
layers it again in vauban-app-layer. getResources gives the parent's
resources, then the loader's own, so VaubanClassLoader returned the record of
the frozen extensions twice, and FrozenExtensions.find took the two results
for two records: the build's work was refused and every extension ran at
start, even in an image whose classes are byte for byte those of the build.

VaubanClassLoader.findResources now leaves out what its parent already
gives, as CompositeClassLoader does, with file:///x and file:/x taken for the
same file. FrozenExtensions.find counts distinct files.

Left: jlink's default --strip-debug changes the class bytes, so the
fingerprint of a stripped image still differs from the build's. That is a
choice between the fingerprint and vidocq:jlink, not part of this fix.

BUG-20261113-17.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DQoEaLnfwGpxVYSXFoFQA8
